mainTopic: Counting multiple sets of lashes for one act, and the start of the משנה on how many lashes are given
overview: The amud opens by finishing the count of five sets of lashes for someone who cooks a גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it. The גמרא asks why kindling counts separately from cooking. It tries replacing kindling with נבילה, then with עצי אשירה, and finally settles on cooking with wood of הקדש. A סימן then introduces six אמוראים who each suggest another prohibition that one act of plowing could break. רבי זעירא and רבי מני then debate whether an oath not to plow on יום טוב should be counted. The final reason it is left out is that this תנא does not hold of איסור כולל. רבי הושעיא and רבי יצחק teach that a פסולי המוקדשין ox counts as two bodies. A new משנה begins: lashes are forty minus one, while רבי יהודה says a full forty. It also starts the rules for estimating how many lashes a person can take, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: How can there be extra lashes for kindling?
steps.stepSummary: If there is no splitting of labors on יום טוב, he should not get separate lashes for kindling, since he is already punished for cooking.
steps.simpleTranslation: The list ends with lashes for kindling. But if that view is right, he should not be liable for kindling, because he is already liable for cooking!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last item on the list in the משנה that אביי quoted, lashes for kindling a fire. It asks how this can count as a separate punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He lit the fire in order to cook. If the labors of יום טוב are not split into separate counts, the kindling is swallowed up by the cooking. So the list seems to count one act twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling a fire
And if it is so (if that view is correct)
His cooking
Is liable (for punishment)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that kindling on יום טוב is permitted. It is only saying that here it cannot be counted as a separate set of lashes on top of the cooking.

phrases.english: for kindling.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if it is true that the labors of יום טוב are not split into separate counts.

phrases.english: he is not liable for kindling,
since he is already liable for his cooking!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, מִשּׁוּם הַבְעָרָה לָא מִחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fifth item (kindling) in the list of lashes in the משנה that אביי quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's counting of a separate set of lashes for הבערה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If labors on יום טוב are not split, the kindling done for cooking is covered by the cooking, so it cannot be punished twice.

steps.title: Replace kindling with a carcass's sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: Take kindling off the list and put in its place that the גיד הנשה came from a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Remove kindling from the list, and put in the גיד הנשה of a נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by swapping out kindling for another prohibition. The case is now a גיד הנשה from an animal that died without proper שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kindling cannot be counted, but the total of five can still work if the eating breaks a third ban, eating נבילה. The count is kept by moving one set of lashes from the cooking side to the eating side.

keyTerms.meaning: Take out, remove
Put in, insert
The sciatic nerve, forbidden to eat
An animal that died without proper שחיטה

phrases.english: Remove kindling
and insert the sciatic nerve of a carcass.
phrases.notes: So eating it also breaks the ban on eating נבילה, which adds another set of lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by replacing kindling with another prohibition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the list: one item is swapped for another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Kindling was one of the five sets of lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifth set comes from eating a גיד הנשה that is also נבילה.

steps.title: רבי חייא's count rules out the carcass answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught two sets of lashes for eating and three for cooking, but the נבילה answer gives three for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא taught that he gets two sets of lashes for eating and three for cooking. If you are right, he would get three for eating!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer using a teaching of רבי חייא that splits the five sets of lashes: two for eating and three for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נבילה the eating side has three bans: גיד הנשה, meat with milk, and נבילה. That leaves only two on the cooking side. This is the reverse of רבי חייא's split, so the fifth item must be about the cooking.

keyTerms.meaning: Is flogged, receives lashes
His eating
Two... three (sets of lashes)

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiya teach:
He is flogged two for his eating
and three for his cooking.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the fifth item really is a גיד הנשה of a נבילה.

phrases.english: he is liable three for his eating!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the נבילה replacement using a ברייתא that splits the count.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion to insert גיד הנשה של נבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא gives three sets for cooking and two for eating. The נבילה answer gives three for eating and two for cooking, so it does not match.

steps.title: Replace kindling with wood of an אשירה
steps.stepSummary: Instead, he cooked with wood of an אשירה, which is forbidden to benefit from, so the extra set of lashes stays on the cooking side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, remove kindling and put in wood of an אשירה. Its warning comes from the פסוק: 'And nothing shall cleave to your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new replacement that belongs to the cooking side: he cooked using wood from a tree that was worshipped as an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using wood of an אשירה as fuel is benefiting from idolatry, which is forbidden. This keeps three bans on the cooking side (cooking on יום טוב, cooking meat with milk, and the אשירה wood), which matches רבי חייא. The גמרא also gives the פסוק that serves as the warning, since lashes need a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood of a tree worshipped as an idol
A warning, the פסוק that sets up the prohibition needed for lashes
From here

phrases.english: Rather: remove kindling
and insert wood of an asheira,
phrases.notes: He cooked the meat using this forbidden wood as fuel.

phrases.english: and its warning is from here:
"And nothing shall cleave to your hand, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אַפֵּיק הַבְעָרָה וְעַיֵּיל עֲצֵי אֲשֵׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new replacement that fits רבי חייא's split of three for cooking.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the case to a different cooking-side prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifth item was נבילה, on the eating side.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifth item is cooking with עצי אשירה, which keeps three sets on the cooking side.

steps.title: אשירה wood would bring a sixth set of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks: with אשירה wood he should also get lashes for 'do not bring an abomination into your house.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: Then he should also be flogged for 'You shall not bring an abomination into your house'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges the אשירה answer. It adds too many prohibitions, which would make the count more than five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing idolatrous wood home breaks another לאו. That would give a sixth set of lashes, but the משנה says five. So the אשירה answer is also a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he should also be flogged
An abomination, here meaning an idolatrous item

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Then let him also be flogged for
"You shall not bring an abomination into your house"!
phrases.notes: דברים 7:26

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the עצי אשירה replacement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that he cooked with עצי אשירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אשירה wood also breaks the ban on bringing an abomination home, which makes six sets instead of five.

steps.title: The case is cooking with wood of הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The case is where he cooked with wood of הקדש. Destroying holy property is forbidden by 'you shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? Where he cooked it with wood of הקדש. Its warning is from the פסוק: 'And their אשרים you shall burn in fire… you shall not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final replacement for kindling: the wood belonged to הקדש. Burning it adds exactly one more ban to the cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells us to burn idols' trees but not to do the same to holy things, so destroying הקדש is a לאו. Unlike אשירה wood, this brings no extra ban about bringing it home. That gives three sets for cooking and two for eating, a total of five, just as רבי חייא taught.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?
Wood that belongs to the בית המקדש
You shall not do so (do not destroy holy things)

steps.whatToRemember: The five sets of lashes are two for eating (eating גיד הנשה, eating meat with milk) and three for cooking (cooking on יום טוב, cooking meat with milk, burning wood of הקדש).

phrases.english: Rather: what are we dealing with here?
Where he cooked it with consecrated wood,
and its warning is from here:
"And their asherim you shall burn in fire…
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3–4. The dots skip the middle of the פסוקים.

phrases.english: you shall not do so to the Lord your God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא by switching from אשירה wood to הקדש wood.
steps.terutzResolutionType: הכא במאי עסקינן: setting the case in a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fifth set came from עצי אשירה, which would really give six.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fifth set comes from burning הקדש wood, which gives exactly five.

steps.title: Memory aid for the next section
steps.stepSummary: A סימן listing the first letters of the אמוראים who will add items in the coming discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: A memory aid: ש-נ-ב-א-י, ש-נ-ז.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next section. It gives a memory aid for the names of the sages whose statements come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters stand for the names הושעיא, חנניה, אבהו, אביי, אשי, רבינא, and זירא. They will each suggest additions to the משנה's list of eight prohibitions for one who plows with כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, letters to help remember the order of the coming statements

phrases.english: A mnemonic.
Shin, Nun, Beit, Alef, Yod; Shin, Nun, Zayin
phrases.notes: Each letter stands for one of the sages coming up next: הושעיא, חנניה, אבהו, אביי, אשי, רבינא, זירא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the גיד הנשה discussion and opens the next topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling here, only a memory aid for the order of the coming statements.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: count sowing in the valley of the עגלה ערופה
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks why the תנא does not also count sowing in the נחל איתן, which the Torah forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא objects: the list should also count someone who sows in the נחל איתן. Its warning comes from the פסוק 'which will not be worked and will not be sown.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא challenges the list of prohibitions you can break with one act of plowing. He says one item is missing: sowing in the נחל איתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נחל איתן is the valley where the עגלה ערופה is brought. The Torah says that land may never be worked or sown again, so plowing or sowing there breaks a לאו. If the תנא is listing every לאו that one act of plowing can break, this one seems to be missing.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (raises a challenge)
Let him also count (in the list)
The harsh valley where the עגלה ערופה is brought
The Torah's warning (the לאו) behind a punishment
The heifer whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the first of six challenges with the same pattern: 'let him also count X, and its warning is from here.' They come from רב הושעיא, רב חנניא, רבי אבהו, אביי, רב אשי and רבינא, and each one adds another item to the plowing list.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya objects to this:
And let him also count
one who sows in the harsh valley,
phrases.notes: This is the valley where the עגלה ערופה was brought, which may never be farmed.

phrases.english: and its warning is from here:
"which will not be worked and will not be sown"!
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the first of the additions hinted at by the סימן in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the תנא's count of prohibitions broken by one act of plowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plowing or sowing in the נחל איתן breaks an explicit לאו, so the list should have included it.

steps.title: רב חנניא: count erasing God's Name while plowing
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא asks why the list does not count someone who erases a written Name of ה׳ as he plows along.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא objects: the list should also count someone who erases God's Name as he goes along. Its warning comes from 'And you shall destroy their name… do not do so to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second challenge with the same pattern. רב חנניא adds erasing שם ה׳ during plowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Name is written on something in the field, the plow can scrape it off. The פסוק tells us to destroy the names of idols but not to treat ה׳ that way, and that is a לאו against erasing His Name. So this is one more prohibition that one furrow could break.

keyTerms.meaning: Erasing a written Name of ה׳
As he goes along (while plowing)
Do not do so (the לאו against destroying holy things)

phrases.english: Rav Chananya objects to this:
And let him also count
one who erases the Name as he goes along,
and its warning is from here:
"And you shall destroy their name, etc.
you shall not do so to ה׳ your God"!
phrases.notes: דברים 12:3–4. Some versions leave out the ו in round brackets, which matches the wording of the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב חֲנַנְיָא: וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a parallel challenge that adds a second missing item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the תנא's count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Erasing the Name while plowing breaks a לאו, so it should have been listed.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: count cutting off a צרעת mark
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks why the list does not count someone who cuts off his בהרת (a white צרעת mark) while plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו objects: the list should also count someone who cuts off his בהרת. Its warning comes from 'Take heed of the plague of צרעת.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third parallel challenge. רבי אבהו adds cutting off a צרעת mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with a בהרת may not remove it to escape טומאה. If the plowing cuts it off, he has broken that לאו. That makes one more prohibition that could happen in the same act.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright white skin mark of צרעת
Cuts off
The affliction of צרעת

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu objects to this:
And let him also count
one who cuts off his white leprous mark,
and its warning is from here:
"Take heed of the plague of leprosy"!
phrases.notes: דברים 24:8

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a parallel challenge that adds a third missing item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the תנא's count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting off a בהרת breaks a לאו and could happen while plowing, so it should be counted.

steps.title: אביי: count loosening the breastplate or removing the Ark's poles
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks why the list does not count loosening the חושן from the אפוד or removing the poles of the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objects: the list should also count someone who loosens the חושן from the אפוד, and someone who removes the poles of the ארון. Their warnings come from 'they shall not be removed' and 'the חושן shall not be loosened.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth challenge in the series. אביי adds two more Torah prohibitions involving the בגדי כהונה and the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives a separate לאו for each case: the poles must never be taken out of the ארון, and the חושן must never come loose from the אפוד. אביי says these too could be broken in the course of plowing. So the list should include them as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן גדול's breastplate
The apron-like garment of the כהן גדול that the חושן is tied to
The carrying poles of the Ark
Loosens, detaches

steps.whatToRemember: So far four אמוראים have each added prohibitions that plowing could break: sowing the נחל איתן, erasing שם ה׳, cutting off a בהרת, and loosening the חושן or removing the ארון's poles. Two more additions follow in steps 12 and 13.

phrases.english: Abaye objects to this:
And let him also count
one who loosens the breastplate from upon the ephod,
and one who removes the poles of the Ark,
and their warning is from here:
"they shall not be removed,"
phrases.notes: שמות 25:15, about the poles. Some versions leave out the ו in round brackets.

phrases.english: "and the breastplate shall not be loosened"!
phrases.notes: שמות 28:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the fourth parallel challenge, and it adds two more missing items.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the תנא's count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Loosening the חושן and removing the ארון's poles each break an explicit לאו that could happen while plowing, so they should be listed.

steps.title: Why not count plowing with wood of an idol-tree?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks why the תנא does not also count plowing with a plow made from the wood of an אשירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: Let the תנא also count someone who plows with wood from an אשירה. Its prohibition comes from the verse: 'And nothing shall cling to your hand…'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds one more prohibition the plower could break, in the same style as the earlier challenges. He asks why the משנה left it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plow made from אשירה wood means he is using something connected to עבודה זרה, which is forbidden. רב אשי even gives the source for the לאו, so this looks like a real extra prohibition the list could have counted.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that is worshipped as עבודה זרה
Wood that comes from an אשירה
The Torah's warning (לאו) that makes something forbidden
'And so on.' The rest of the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to this:
And let him also count
one who plows with wood of an asheira,
and its prohibition is from here:
"And nothing shall cling to your hand, etc."!
phrases.notes: דברים 13:18

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another addition in the series of challenges listed in the סימן
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list of prohibitions in one act of plowing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Using אשירה wood is a separate לאו that happens during the plowing, so the list seems incomplete

steps.title: Why not count cutting down good fruit trees?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks why the תנא does not count someone who chops down good fruit trees while plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objects: Let the תנא also count someone who cuts down good trees. Its prohibition comes from the verse: 'For you may eat from it, but you shall not cut it down.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds another prohibition that could happen during the same plowing. This is the last of the simple additions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the plow cuts through good fruit trees, he breaks the Torah's ban on destroying them. רבינא supplies the פסוק, so it seems the list should include this too.

keyTerms.meaning: One who chops down or cuts off
Good trees, meaning fruit-bearing trees
'Do not cut down.' The Torah's ban on destroying fruit trees

phrases.english: Ravina objects to this:
And let him also count
one who chops down good trees,
phrases.notes: Good trees here means fruit trees that he cuts down as he plows.

phrases.english: and its prohibition is from here:
"For you may eat from it,
phrases.notes: דברים 20:19

phrases.english: and you shall not cut it down"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same style of challenge as רב אשי's
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting fruit trees is another לאו that can happen in the same act of plowing

steps.title: Why not count an oath not to plow on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירא asks רבי מני why the list does not include someone who swore not to plow on יום טוב and then plowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said to רבי מני: Let the תנא also count a case where someone said, 'I swear that I will not plow on יום טוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new kind of challenge begins. This time the added prohibition comes from the person's own oath, not straight from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone swears not to plow on יום טוב and then plows, he seems to break his שבועה on top of the יום טוב prohibition already in the משנה. So רבי זעירא suggests the list could have one more לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath. Breaking it is a Torah prohibition
A Festival, when plowing is forbidden
I will plow

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זְעֵירָא לְרַבִּי מָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Mani:
And let him also count
a case where one said:
"An oath that I will not plow on the Festival"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זְעֵירָא לְרַבִּי מָנִי וְלִיחְשׁוֹב נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from Torah-given prohibitions to a prohibition the person creates with an oath
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the משנה's list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An oath adds its own prohibition on top of the יום טוב ban

steps.title: The oath does not take effect: he is already sworn from סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני answers that this oath never takes effect, because the person is already bound from הר סיני not to plow on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the oath does not take effect, because he is already sworn from הר סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני answers the challenge. Swearing to keep a rule the Torah already gave does nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already forbids plowing on יום טוב, so the person counts as 'already under oath from סיני.' A new oath cannot take hold on something he is already bound by, so it adds no extra prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes effect, takes hold
Already under oath from הר סיני, meaning already bound by the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying the oath is a sin or forbidden to make. It just has no legal effect, so it adds no new prohibition.

phrases.english: There, the oath does not take effect,
he is already sworn from Mount Sinai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זעירא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal principle: an oath cannot take effect on an existing Torah obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath adds a separate prohibition
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath is empty, so there is nothing to count

steps.title: An oath covering weekdays too would also take hold on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי זעירא pushes back with an oath that includes weekdays and יום טוב together, so it does take effect on יום טוב as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Take a case where he said, 'I swear I will not plow, whether on a weekday or on יום טוב.' Since the oath takes effect on weekdays, it also takes effect on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זעירא renews his challenge by improving the case. Now the oath does work on יום טוב too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On weekdays plowing is allowed, so the oath clearly takes hold there. Using מגו ('since'), once the oath takes hold for weekdays it also takes hold for יום טוב, so the problem from the previous step is solved and the extra prohibition is back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since.' Because it works in one part, it works in the other part too
A regular weekday
Whether... or. Both cases together

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבי זעירא answering back.

phrases.english: For example, where one said:
"An oath that I will not plow
whether on a weekday or on the Festival,"
for since the oath takes effect on him on a weekday,
it takes effect on him on the Festival as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ כְּגוֹן דְּאָמַר שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אֶחְרוֹשׁ בֵּין בַּחוֹל בֵּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the answer in step 15 by making the oath also cover weekdays
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מני's answer that the oath does not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With מגו the oath does take hold on יום טוב, so there is a real extra prohibition

steps.title: The תנא does not count things that can be released by a חכם
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני answers that the תנא does not list anything that can be undone through שאילה, and oaths can be undone that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא does not teach anything that can be undone by asking a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני gives a new reason for leaving the oath out. He does not argue with the מגו at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועה can be released by going to a חכם (שאילה), so it is not a fixed prohibition. The תנא only lists prohibitions that cannot be removed this way. This sets up a rule that the גמרא will now test against the משנה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Asking a חכם to release a vow or oath
Something, a matter
He does not teach it, it is not in the list

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what the next steps test. Any item in the משנה that seems releasable must be explained.

phrases.english: A matter that is subject to release by request
phrases.notes: He means something a חכם can cancel when the person asks to be released.

phrases.english: he does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the improved challenge with a new principle about the list
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines what kind of item the תנא includes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any prohibition that applies during the plowing belongs in the list
steps.terutzMaskana: Only prohibitions that cannot be released by a חכם are listed

steps.title: But the משנה counts הקדש, which can be released
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new rule: the משנה counts consecrated animals, and consecration can be undone by a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does it not? But there is הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבי מני's rule against the משנה. The משנה includes plowing with consecrated animals, and consecration starts with a vow that a חכם can release.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא never counts releasable things, why does he count הקדש? Making an animal holy is a kind of vow, so it seems a חכם could undo it. That would go against the rule from step 17.

keyTerms.meaning: Something consecrated, given to the בית המקדש
'But look at...' Used to bring a challenge from a case

phrases.english: And does he not?
But there is consecrated property!
phrases.notes: The משנה counts plowing with consecrated animals, and a חכם can release a consecration vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just given in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the תנא leaves out anything releasable by שאילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הקדש is releasable, yet the משנה lists it

steps.title: The consecrated animal is a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה is talking about a בכור, which is holy from birth and was never made holy by a vow, so no חכם can release it.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the consecrated animal in the משנה is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור becomes holy by itself at birth, not because a person vowed it. Since there was no vow, there is nothing for a חכם to release, so the rule from step 17 still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, holy from birth

phrases.english: With a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הקדש challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The הקדש in the משנה came from a vow and can be released
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a בכור, which cannot be released

steps.title: But the משנה counts a נזיר, and נזירות can be released
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the משנה counts a נזיר who becomes טמא, and a vow of נזירות can be released by a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the rule again with another item in the משנה, the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נזירות starts with a vow, and a חכם can release vows. So counting a נזיר seems to break the rule that releasable things are not listed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who vowed נזירות and may not become טמא from the dead

phrases.english: But there is a nazirite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the same rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that releasable items are not counted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נזירות is a vow that can be released, yet the משנה lists the נזיר

steps.title: The נזיר is a נזיר שמשון
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה means a נזיר שמשון, whose נזירות cannot be released, so the rule stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a Samson-type nazirite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the נזיר in the משנה is a נזיר שמשון, which would save רבי מני's rule. The next step rejects this answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר שמשון is a special kind of נזירות, and the answer here is that it cannot be released by a חכם. So both items in the משנה that looked releasable turn out to be cases that cannot be released.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזירות modeled on שמשון, which a חכם cannot release

phrases.english: With a Samson-type nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the נזיר challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The נזיר in the משנה has an ordinary נזירות that can be released
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a נזיר שמשון, which cannot be released

steps.title: A נזיר שמשון may become impure from the dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer that the משנה means a נזיר שמשון. Such a נזיר is allowed to become impure from a corpse, so he could not be the one the משנה counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a נזיר שמשון forbidden to become impure from the dead? He is not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from the last step. A נזיר שמשון is allowed to become טמא to the dead, so he cannot be the נזיר the משנה is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives lashes to a נזיר for becoming טמא from the dead. A נזיר שמשון has no such איסור, so the משנה must mean a regular נזיר. A regular נזיר's vow can be undone by a חכם, so רבי מני's rule (nothing that can be undone is listed) breaks down again.

keyTerms.meaning: A lifelong נזיר modeled on שמשון. His נזירות cannot be undone, and he may become impure from the dead.
To become impure (טמא)
The dead; impurity from a corpse

phrases.english: A nazir like Samson —
is he subject to the ban on becoming impure from the dead?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְזִיר שִׁמְשׁוֹן בַּר אִיטַּמּוֹיֵי לְמֵתִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה's נזיר is a נזיר שמשון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה punishes the נזיר for corpse impurity, but a נזיר שמשון has no such איסור. So the case must be a regular נזיר, whose vow can be undone.

steps.title: This תנא does not accept an inclusive prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רבי מני's approach. It explains instead that the oath is left out because this תנא does not hold of איסור כולל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this תנא does not hold of an 'inclusive prohibition'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand-new reason why the משנה did not count the oath not to plow on weekdays and on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is already bound from סיני not to plow on יום טוב, so an oath about יום טוב alone does not take hold. One could argue that adding weekdays makes a wider oath, which then takes hold on יום טוב too. This is איסור כולל. This תנא rejects that idea, so the oath adds no extra לאו on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'inclusive prohibition': a wider איסור that takes hold even where an איסור already exists, because it also covers new ground
He does not hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, the oath is missing from the משנה's list because this תנא does not hold of איסור כולל. It is not because oaths can be undone.

phrases.english: Rather,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תַּנָּא אִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל לֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: this tanna does not hold of an inclusive prohibition.
phrases.notes: He means the oath against plowing on weekdays and on יום טוב. It can't take hold on יום טוב, which is already forbidden from סיני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed approach of steps 17–21 with a new answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the underlying principle (the תנא's view on איסור כולל)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The oath was left out because oaths can be undone by a חכם
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath was left out because, for this תנא, a wider oath cannot take hold on top of the existing יום טוב איסור

steps.title: Breeding a disqualified sacred ox gets two sets of lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא rules that someone who breeds a disqualified sacred ox gets lashes twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא said: one who breeds a disqualified sacred ox gets lashes twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי הושעיא about a redeemed sacred animal, adding to the list of extra לאווים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסולי המוקדשין animal stays forbidden for work even after it is redeemed, so that is one set of lashes. The Torah also treats it like two bodies, holy and ordinary, so breeding it counts as כלאים. That is the second set.

keyTerms.meaning: One who breeds (mates) animals
Sacred animals that became unfit (blemished) and were redeemed
Gets two sets of lashes

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya says:
One who breeds a disqualified consecrated ox
is flogged two times.
phrases.notes: One set is for using the sacred animal, and the other is for כלאים, mixing kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching related to the topic of extra לאווים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breeding a פסולי המוקדשין ox brings two sets of lashes

steps.title: Driving a disqualified sacred ox counts as two bodies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rules that driving a disqualified sacred ox brings lashes, because the Torah treats one body as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: one who drives a disqualified sacred ox gets lashes, because it is one body that the Torah made into two bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a parallel teaching. Even working with this one ox alone can count as mixing two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally כלאים in work needs two animals of different kinds. Here the Torah treats the one redeemed sacred ox like two bodies, holy and ordinary. So driving it alone is like working with two kinds together.

keyTerms.meaning: One who drives or leads an animal at work
One body
Two bodies

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the idea behind רבי הושעיא's ruling: a פסולי המוקדשין animal counts like two separate bodies.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak says:
One who drives a disqualified consecrated ox
is flogged,
for it is one body,
and the verse made it like two bodies.
phrases.notes: The holy part and the ordinary part count separately, so it is like plowing with two kinds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling based on the same idea as step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Driving a פסולי המוקדשין ox brings lashes, because it counts as two bodies

steps.title: Lashes are forty minus one
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that lashes are thirty-nine. It learns this from reading the words 'by number, forty' as a number close to forty.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many lashes do we give him? Forty minus one, as it says, 'by number, forty': a number close to forty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the number of lashes at thirty-nine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה joins the last word of one פסוק ('by number') to the first word of the next ('forty'). It reads them as 'the number that comes right before forty,' which is thirty-nine.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
We give lashes
Forty minus one, which is thirty-nine
Next to, close to

steps.confusionAlert: The Torah says 'forty,' yet the הלכה is thirty-nine. The משנה gets this by reading 'by number, forty' as 'the number right next to forty.'

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How many lashes do they give him?
Forty less one,
as it is stated: 'By number, forty' —
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2–3

phrases.english: a number that is adjacent to forty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lashes are thirty-nine, learned from 'by number, forty'

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a full forty lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the punishment is a full forty lashes. The extra one is given between the shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he gets a full forty. And where does he get the extra one? Between his shoulders.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the first opinion of the משנה and gives his own number and placement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lashes are split into three places on the body. Thirty-nine splits evenly into three, so the fortieth lash is left over. רבי יהודה says it goes between the shoulders.

keyTerms.meaning: Full, complete
The extra one
Between his shoulders

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He is flogged with a full forty,
and where is he flogged the extra one?
Between his shoulders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full forty lashes, with the extra one between the shoulders

steps.title: Assessments must divide into three
steps.stepSummary: When estimating how many lashes he can survive, the number used must be one that splits evenly into three.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only estimate him using a number of lashes that can be divided into three.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה teaches how to set a smaller number of lashes for someone too weak for the full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lashes are given in three equal parts, so any estimate must be a multiple of three. If he can take twenty, for example, he gets eighteen.

keyTerms.meaning: We estimate, assess (how much he can take)
To be divided into three

phrases.english: They do not assess him
except with lashes fit to be divided into three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about lowering the number of lashes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An assessment of lashes must be a number divisible by three

steps.title: Assessed for forty, but some were already given
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new case: he was assessed as able to take forty, and some of the lashes were already given.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they assessed him as able to take forty, and he was given some of them...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up a case whose ruling comes in the next part of the משנה. It opens the question of what happens when he gets weak partway through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case: he was judged strong enough for the full amount, and the beating has started. The ruling has not been given yet; the משנה finishes it next.

keyTerms.meaning: They assessed him
Some, part

phrases.english: If they assessed him to receive forty,
phrases.notes: 'Forty' here means the full set of thirty-nine lashes.

phrases.english: and he is flogged some of them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a new case about the assessment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up here; the ruling comes next
